title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', his study of the loop equation from the Longue Marche. He studies, in GL_2 over a base (points written Γ, Γ = sections), the solution scheme of a commutator equation. The unknowns are (α, β, μ) plus signs ε, ε'. The data are fixed elements ρ and σ. The equation is roughly [α,ρ] = ε[β,σ]ε^{-1}, with an extra (μ−1) term whose exact form is partly illegible.

Notation fixed on the previous page:
- T_ρ and T_σ are the centralizers (maximal tori) of ρ and σ.
- N'_σ is a normalizer-type extension of T_σ by elements sending σ to −σ. Getting ε = −1 locally needs Tr σ = 0.
- B'_0 is a Borel subgroup and T_0 = B'_0 ∩ B'_1 = {diag(μ,1)} is its privileged torus.
- G*_{ρ,σ} is given a group-scheme structure by transporting the product group structure along a parametrization G*_{ρ,σ} ≅ B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, written (u,a,b).
- G*_{ρ,σ}(0) corresponds to T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ.
- G^♮(0) = G_{ρ,σ} ∩ G*(0) corresponds to T_0 × T_ρ × T_σ.

On this page.
- (16)–(17): Since B'_0 = L_0 ⋊ T_0, with L_0 the unipotent radical, one gets semidirect product decompositions G* ≅ G*(0)·Λ_0, and likewise for the unstarred version. Here Λ_0 = {(α=λ, β=λ, μ=1) : λ ∈ L_0}, with λ = ε_0^n and ε_0 the standard unipotent [[1,1],[0,1]]. Λ_0 lies in G_{ρ,σ} and corresponds to L_0 × {1} × {1}. It is the 'diagonal' unipotent family: α = β = λ solves the equation trivially in this normalization.
- (18): Grothendieck defines the subgroup scheme SG*_{ρ,σ} by (det α)^2 = 1 and det β = 1.
- (19): Equivalently, SG* is the scheme of systems (α, β, μ, ε, ε') with the commutator relation, det α = ε', det β = 1 and ε^2 = ε'^2 = 1. He remarks that ε^2 = 1 already follows from the first relation, by taking determinants.
- (20): In the coordinates (u,a,b), the conditions reduce to det u = det b = ε' det a with ε'^2 = 1.

The next page checks that SG* is a subgroup containing Λ_0 (the case ε' = 1, all determinants 1). It deduces SG* ≅ SG*(0)·Λ_0, reducing the structure of SG* to a subgroup of the torus-like group T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ.

Purpose: an explicit structure theory of the group of solutions of the loop/commutator equation in GL_2 / SL_2. Presumably this serves the description of the GL_2 or SL_2 points of the Lego / Teichmüller-tower relations, or of 'reduced' loop equations.
errors: The semidirect product is written G*(0)·Λ_0. The normal factor should be Λ_0, coming from L_0 normal in B'_0. Since the order of factors is only notational, this is harmless.
The parameter n of λ = ε_0^n should range over Γ(G_a), not Γ(G_m), because L_0 is unipotent. Either Grothendieck or the transcription has a slip here.

ideas.what: Group-scheme structure on the solution scheme of a commutator ('loop') equation, by transport of structure from B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, with a semidirect decomposition by the unipotent diagonal subgroup Λ_0
ideas.modern_name: Solution scheme of a word equation in GL_2 / representation-variety computation; Levi decomposition B = T ⋉ U

ideas.what: Special subgroup SG* cut out by determinant conditions (det α = ±1, det β = 1), with the sign ε' tracking det α
ideas.modern_name: SL_2 / determinant-restricted subgroup of a solution group

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping of algebraic-group structure (Levi decomposition, determinant conditions) inside a longer computation on the loop equation. There is no new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: In (17), 'n ∈ Γ G_m' should probably read 'n ∈ Γ G_a', since L_0 is unipotent.
In (16), the second isomorphism most likely involves the ♮ version: G_{ρ,σ} ≃ G^♮_{ρ,σ}(0)·Λ_0, consistent with definition (15) on the previous page. It is not a 'G^{**}' object.
In (19), the first relation reads approximately [α,ρ] = ε[β,σ]ε^{-1} with a (μ−1) term attached. The transcription 'ε[β,σ]ε,(μ-1)' is garbled.
'Donc [?]' before 'comme la solution' is likely 'Donc' written above the struck 'Soit donc'.
'dans le premier cas notamment [?]' is likely 'dans le premier cas notamment' or similar. The phrase is poorly legible.
